# Background

We conducted this experiment to study the allelopathic effect of MBOA on Arabidopsis growth. We looked at both root inhibition on plates and growth inhibition in soil.

# Materials and methods

-   **Plant material**: Arabidopsis thaliana

-   **Genotypes**: Col-0 and the most extreme accessions

-   **Treatment**: MBOA

-   **Phenotypes**: Root length, plant area

-   **Accessions**: See list of plant genotypes used in GWAS

-   **Purpose**: We performed this study to test the sensitvity of the most extreme accessions to MBOA.

# Important results

MBOA show similar effects to all the accessions, irrespective of their growth feedbacks

### Helper Functions

```{r echo=TRUE, message=FALSE}
# Function to display the number of replicates below each bar
give.n <- function(x){
  return(c(y = median(x) * -0.005, label = length(x)))
}

# Function to make colored facets at the bottom
element_textbox_highlight <- function(..., 
                                      hi.labels = NULL, hi.fill = NULL,
                                      hi.col = NULL, hi.box.col = NULL,
                                      hi.labels2 = NULL, hi.fill2 = NULL,
                                      hi.col2 = NULL, hi.box.col2 = NULL) {
  structure(
    c(element_textbox(...),
      list(hi.labels = hi.labels, hi.fill = hi.fill, hi.col = hi.col, hi.box.col = hi.box.col,
           hi.labels2 = hi.labels2, hi.fill2 = hi.fill2, 
           hi.col2 = hi.col2, hi.box.col2 = hi.box.col2)
    ),
    class = c("element_textbox_highlight", "element_textbox", "element_text", "element")
  )
}

element_grob.element_textbox_highlight <- function(element, label = "", ...) {
  if (label %in% element$hi.labels) {
    element$fill <- element$hi.fill %||% element$fill
    element$colour <- element$hi.col %||% element$colour
    element$box.colour <- element$hi.box.col %||% element$box.colour
  }
  if (label %in% element$hi.labels2) {
    element$fill <- element$hi.fill2 %||% element$fill
    element$colour <- element$hi.col2 %||% element$colour
    element$box.colour <- element$hi.box.col2 %||% element$box.colour
  }
  NextMethod()
}
```

-   **Purpose**: We defined two helper functions to display the number of replicates below each bar in the boxplot and to create colored facets at the bottom of the plot.

# Anova test of Root Length response to MBOA

```{r}
root_length$treatment <- as.factor(root_length$treatment)
root_length$accession <- as.factor(root_length$accession)
root_length$response <- as.factor(root_length$response)

# Perform ANOVA
anova_results <- aov(root_length ~ treatment * accession , data = root_length)
summary(anova_results)

# Perform post hoc tests for each genotype (accession)
posthoc_results <- emmeans::emmeans(anova_results, ~ treatment | accession)
pairwise_comparisons <- emmeans::contrast(posthoc_results, method = "pairwise", adjust = "bonferroni")
pairwise_summary <- summary(pairwise_comparisons)

# Display pairwise comparison results
kable(pairwise_summary, caption = "Pairwise Comparisons of Root Length by Treatment and Accessions")
#print(pairwise_summary)
```

```{r}
# Extract p-values from the post hoc results
p_values_df <- pairwise_summary %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    label = sprintf("p = %.3g", p.value),  # Format p-values as text labels
    treatment_pair = paste(contrast)  # Combine treatment names for annotation
  )

# Plot with p-values for post hoc tests
plot_root_length <- ggplot(root_length, aes(x = treatment, y = root_length)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(fill = treatment),
    size = 0.3,
    alpha = 0.5,
    notch = FALSE,
    outlier.size = 1.0
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange2", "red4")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5.0)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = factor(treatment)),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0),
    shape = 20,
    alpha = 0.2,
    size = 0.5,
    stroke = 1,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Treatment",
    y = "Root length (cm)",
    title = "Root Length by Treatment and Accessions"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, colour = "black"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(accession, levels = c(
    "IP-Hue-3", "Tac-0", "Dra2-1", "DraIV 3-7", 
    "Bozen-1.2", "Kastel-1", "Col-0", "Hadd-3", 
    "Rak-2", "T840", "Lm-2", "BRR60", "Giffo-1"
  )), nrow = 2) +
  # Annotate with p-values from post hoc tests
  geom_text(
    data = p_values_df,
    aes(
      x = 1.5,  # Adjust x position (centered between treatments)
      y = 4.5,  # Adjust y position to place labels above the boxplots
      label = label
    ),
    color = "black",
    size = 3,
    hjust = 0.5
  )

# Display the plot
print(plot_root_length)
# Save the plot as a PDF
ggsave("MBOA_accessions_root_length.pdf", plot_root_length, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 600,path = "Output/Figures/")
```

-   **Result**: MBOA inhibits root growth in all accessions, irrespective of their growth feedback. The root length is significantly reduced in the MBOA treatment compared to the control.

# Treatment response

```{r}
library(ggrepel)
# Summarize the average root length for each accession and treatment
avg_root_length <- root_length %>%
  group_by(accession, treatment, response) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_root_length = mean(root_length, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

# Define a named vector of colors for the response variable
response_colors <- c(
  "positive" = "#0072B2",
  "negative" = "orange2" # Add more colors as needed for your responses
)

plot_avg_root_length <- ggplot(avg_root_length, aes(x = treatment, 
                                                    y = mean_root_length,
                                                    group = accession)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = response), size = 1) + # Line connecting points
  geom_point(aes(color = response), size = 2) + # Points for averages
  geom_text_repel(
    data = avg_root_length %>% filter(treatment == "MBOA"), # Filter for "control" treatment
    aes(label = accession, color = "black"), # Add labels with matching colors
    nudge_x = 0.3, # Nudges text horizontally away from the point
    nudge_y = 0,  # Nudges text vertically
    size = 3, # Text size
    segment.size = 0.2, # Line thickness connecting text and point
    segment.color = "grey50", # Line color
    max.overlaps = 3.5 # Limits overlap of labels
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = response_colors) + # Apply the custom colors
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Average Root Length by Treatment for Each Accession",
    x = "Treatment",
    y = "Average Root Length (cm)",
    color = "Response" # Legend title for response
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8)
  )

# Display the plot
print(plot_avg_root_length)
```

# Filter Data for Specific Genotypes

```{r}
#| echo: true
# List of specific genotype_ids
selected_genotypes <- c(9851, 7350, 5867, 5921, 9972, 10006, 
                        6909, 9392, 8365, 6136, 7217, 506, 9653)

# Filter the data for 'dag' = 15 and selected 'genotype_id'
filtered_data <- plant_region_ares_GWAS %>%
  filter(dag == 15, genotype_id %in% selected_genotypes)

# Display the filtered data
kable(
  filtered_data[1:3, ],
  caption = "Extreme contrasting Accessions at DAG = 15"
)
# Save filtered_data as xls document
library(openxlsx)
write.xlsx(filtered_data, "Output/Tables/accession_rosette_areaDAG15.xlsx")
```

-   **Purpose**: We filtered the `plant_region_ares_GWAS` data frame to include only the rows where `dag` is equal to 15 and the `genotype_id` is one of the selected genotypes.

## Calculate and Merge Average Values

```{r, echo=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE}
# Calculate the average plant_region_area for each genotype_id and bx
average_area <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(genotype_id, bx) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(avg_plant_region_area = mean(plant_region_area, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Spread the data to wide format to have separate columns for 'bx' plus and minus
average_area_wide <- average_area %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = bx, values_from = avg_plant_region_area)

# Calculate the response by subtracting 'bx' minus from 'bx' plus
average_area_wide <- average_area_wide %>%
  mutate(response = `+` - `-`)

# Display the resulting data frame
kable(
  average_area_wide[1:3, ],
  caption = "Rosette area of extreme contrasting Accessions at DAG = 15"
)


# Step 1: Calculate the average root_length for each accession_id and treatment
average_root_length <- root_length %>%
  group_by(accession_id, treatment) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(avg_root_length = mean(root_length, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 2: Reshape the data to wide format to separate 'control' and 'MBOA' treatments
average_root_length_wide <- average_root_length %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = avg_root_length)

# Step 3: Calculate the treatment response (Control - MBOA)
average_root_length_wide <- average_root_length_wide %>%
  mutate(treatment_response = MBOA - control)

# Replace "Col_0" with "6909" in the 'accession_id' column
average_root_length_wide <- average_root_length_wide %>%
  mutate(accession_id = ifelse(accession_id == "Col_0", "6909", accession_id))

# Display the resulting data frame
kable(
  average_root_length_wide[1:3, ],
  caption = "Root lenght of extreme contrasting Accessions in response to MBOA"
)

```

-   **Purpose**: We calculated the average plant region area for each genotype and BX treatment and then calculated the response by subtracting the BX minus values from the BX plus values. We also calculated the average root length for each accession and treatment and calculated the treatment response by subtracting the MBOA values from the control values.

## Merge Data and Calculate Correlation

```{r}
#| echo: true
# Convert 'genotype_id' to character in 'average_area_wide' and rename to 'accession_id'
average_area_wide <- average_area_wide %>%
  mutate(genotype_id = as.character(genotype_id)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(accession_id = genotype_id)

# Ensure 'accession_id' in 'average_root_length_wide' is character
average_root_length_wide <- average_root_length_wide %>%
  mutate(accession_id = as.character(accession_id))

# Merge the two tables on 'accession_id'
merged_data <- inner_join(average_root_length_wide, average_area_wide, 
                          by = "accession_id")

# Assign colors based on the response value
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  mutate(feedback = ifelse(response > 0, "BXplus", "BXminus"))


# Calculate the correlation and p-value
cor_test <- cor.test(merged_data$treatment_response, merged_data$response,
                     use = "complete.obs")
correlation <- cor_test$estimate
p_value <- cor_test$p.value

# Print the correlation and p-value
print(paste("Correlation: ", round(correlation, 2)))
print(paste("P-value: ", p_value))
```

-   **Purpose**: We merged the `average_root_length_wide` and `average_area_wide` data frames on the `accession_id` column and assigned colors based on the response value. We then calculated the correlation between the treatment response and the response values and the associated p-value.

-   **Result**: The correlation between the treatment response and the response values is 0.485, with a p-value of 0.092. This indicates that there is no correlation between the two variables.

### Plot Correlation and Treatment Response

```{r}
#| label: Fig-MBOA_response
#| echo: true


# Add the "accession" column to merged_data based on accession_id
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  mutate(accession = root_length$accession[match(accession_id, root_length$accession_id)])

# Reorder accession_id based on response
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  mutate(accession = fct_reorder(accession, response))

# Ensure feedback is a factor with correct levels
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  mutate(feedback = factor(feedback, levels = c("BXplus", "BXminus")))

# Define custom color mapping
feedback_colors <- c("BXminus" = "orange2", "BXplus" = "#0072B2")

# Plot the correlation
plot_correlation <- ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = treatment_response, 
                                            y = response)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = feedback), size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", col = "red4") +
  labs(
    x = "Root Length Response to MBOA",
    y = expression("Growth feedback (10"^4*")"),
    title = "Correlation Analysis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.6),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 7)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = feedback_colors) + 
  annotate(
    "text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, 
    label = paste("r =", round(correlation, 2), "\nP =", 
                  format.pval(p_value, digits = 2)), 
    hjust = 1.1, vjust = -1.1, size = 5, color = "black"
  )

# Plot the treatment response
treatment_response_plot <- ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = treatment_response, 
                                                   y = accession)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = feedback), size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red4", size = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Root Length Response to MBOA",
    y = "Accessions",
    title = "Treatment Response of Each Accession"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.6),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = feedback_colors)  # Same color scheme as first plot

# Display the plots
print(plot_correlation)
print(treatment_response_plot)
```

-   **Purpose**: We plotted the correlation between the treatment response and the response values and the treatment response of each accession. The correlation plot shows the relationship between the treatment response and the response values, while the treatment response plot shows the response of each accession to the treatment.

```{r}
#| include: false

combined_plot <- plot_grid(treatment_response_plot, plot_correlation, nrow = 1, labels = c("B.", "C."), label_size = 12)

# Display the combined plot
print(combined_plot)

# Save the combined plot as a PDF
ggsave("MBOA_growth_correlation.pdf", combined_plot, width = 12, height = 5, dpi = 600,path = "Output/Figures/")
```
